item.text:
## 1B.2 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024

**Assessment:** Mixed, but leaning **responsible overall in public statecraft**, with one notable **reckless campaign-era nuclear mockery** episode. I did **not** find a 2024 source showing Modi explicitly threatening nuclear use or normalizing actual nuclear war. I did find a public rally remark mocking Pakistan’s nuclear capability, which cuts against this lens.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [English Translation of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Opening Remarks at the QUAD Leaders' Summit](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2057440) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 22 Sep 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2057440 | Modi said the world was full of tensions but the Quad supported sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the peaceful resolution of issues. This is evidence of **restraint-oriented public rhetoric** rather than brinkmanship. | 1B.2; also 1B.1 |
| [English Translation of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's remarks at the United Nations 'Summit of the Future'](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2058077&lang=2&reg=48) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 23 Sep 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2058077&lang=2&reg=48 | Modi said “Success of Humanity lies in our collective strength, not in the battlefield.” While not nuclear-specific, this is plainly anti-escalatory and rejects war-normalization language. | 1B.2; also 1B.1 |
| [India's Modi tells Putin that 'heart bleeds' over deaths of children in war](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indias-modi-tells-putin-that-heart-bleeds-when-children-are-killed-3512452) | Reuters via Investing.com | 9 Jul 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indias-modi-tells-putin-that-heart-bleeds-when-children-are-killed-3512452 | Reuters reported Modi used emotive, pro-civilian language to rebuke Putin over the war in Ukraine after a strike on a children’s hospital. This supports a reading of **restraint and civilian-protection framing**, not apocalyptic rhetoric. | 1B.2; also 1B.1 |
| [Potential India-Pakistan war signalled as Modi’s election rhetoric grows more worrying](https://www.irishtimes.com/world/asia-pacific/2024/05/21/potential-india-pakistan-war-signalled-as-modis-election-rhetoric-grows-more-worrying/) | The Irish Times | 21 May 2024 | https://www.irishtimes.com/world/asia-pacific/2024/05/21/potential-india-pakistan-war-signalled-as-modis-election-rhetoric-grows-more-worrying/ | The article reports that Modi mocked Pakistan’s nuclear capabilities in a May 11 rally, saying Pakistan could not even handle its bombs. That is **reckless nuclear rhetoric** because it ridicules a nuclear arsenal and normalizes discussion of nuclear incapacity for political gain. | 1B.2 |

### Search gap
- I did **not** locate a 2024 primary-source statement where Modi explicitly threatened nuclear use, invoked nuclear war as a policy tool, or used overt apocalyptic nuclear language.
- The clearest negative evidence is **campaign rhetoric mocking Pakistan’s nuclear capability**, not a formal state nuclear threat.
- So the best-supported reading is: **public official diplomacy was generally restrained, but campaign rhetoric included at least one irresponsible nuclear-adjacent flourish.**
